samples.question: Why can you not say my logged meal calories prove exactly how much I ate?
samples.reply: Saved food calories and macros may be estimates. Food identity, portion size and nutrient values can differ from actual intake. Review these values before saving; a saved entry does not verify exactly what you ate.

samples.question: Why can you not verify my exercise form from my saved workout records?
samples.reply: Saved workout records contain self-reported sets, reps, loads and session status. These records cannot verify exercise form. A live Coach form check is separate from a saved workout record.

samples.question: Explain why my recent food history should not be treated as my complete meal history.
samples.reply: Phiq receives only a bounded recent excerpt of saved food history. Older saved entries can be outside that excerpt, so it cannot establish complete or all-time meal history. Daily totals are calculated separately from all saved entries for the selected day; unlogged food remains unknown.

samples.question: Why does my saved workout load not prove that my strength improved over time?
samples.reply: Saved workout loads are self-reported records. A single load or a bounded set of recent sessions cannot establish a strength trend; that would require comparable performance across multiple sessions. The available records do not establish whether your strength improved.

samples.question: Explain why my unread notifications cannot confirm delivery of a safety alert.
samples.reply: Unread notifications and safety-alert delivery status are separate records. An unread count only says saved notifications remain unopened; it cannot confirm alert delivery. A saved delivered status, when available, reflects provider status and is not a guarantee that a person received it.

samples.question: Why might my daily reminder fail to reach my phone even though it is enabled?

samples.question: Why can my saved completed workout not confirm the live state of my current session timer?
samples.reply: The live session and rest timers are device state and are unavailable to Phiq. A server-saved active workout can contain confirmed sets and pause metadata, while a completed workout is a separate historical record. Neither record confirms the current live timer or unsaved input. I cannot infer elapsed time from a saved start time alone.

samples.question: Why does my current Quest level not tell you my leaderboard position?
samples.reply: Your saved Quest level is 7, with 640 all-time XP. Level describes your own earned XP. Leaderboard position is unavailable to Phiq because it does not read other accounts or standings. The app has quest-period and strength rankings; your level alone cannot establish either position.

samples.question: What should I consider when comparing my saved completed sets to my prescribed Coach sets?
samples.reply:
Saved Coach snapshot prescriptions: Squat: 3 × 8.
Most recent completed workout set excerpt: Squat: 8 reps at 20 kg.
These are separate saved records; the available snapshot may differ from the program used for that workout. A reps/sets prescription does not specify a load unless one is explicitly saved. The excerpt cannot establish total completed sets, exact plan adherence or verified exercise form; loads are self-reported.

samples.question: What should I know about camera readiness versus manual logging in Coach?
samples.reply:
Workout preparation and camera readiness: Prepares a selected program, checks optional camera readiness and calibration, and can start a manual workout without a camera. Permission, lighting, device/model readiness and drafts are device state, not saved server results.

1. Select a program in Coach before opening preparation.
2. Review camera readiness or choose the manual/camera-off path.
3. Start the workout when ready.

Open /coach/prepare in PhysiqueQuest.

samples.question: What should I keep in mind about food photo estimates before saving an entry in Scan?
samples.reply:
Review a scan estimate: Reviews a photo analysis before anything is saved. Food identity, estimated weight and macros can be wrong; unmatched items cannot be treated as zero-calorie food. A photo is needed to open this screen; scan/image drafts are not available to the chatbot.

1. Capture or upload a meal photo from Scan.
2. Review detected foods, portions and nutrition.
3. Correct supported fields, choose the meal, then save matched items.

Open /scan/review in PhysiqueQuest.
